doc.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Louis Armstrong, Basie and New York studio scene
title: Neighbors with Count Basie in St. Albans and a basement with Chaplin films
summary: After leaving Cab, Hinton lived near Basie; Basie escaped his wife's social events to watch silent films and play piano in Hinton's basement.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Wait a minute now. I missed something here. Did you… Basie is after Cab Calloway? You worked with Basie after Cab Calloway?
Yeah after Cab Calloway, I bought a house out here.
So now I am living out here and Basie is out here. Katherine is a very social lady and I am just a bass player. In fact to this very day she always calls me
[Unintelligible] Hilton‟s husband. I wasn‟t into this society at all and Basie wasn‟t either because he was like the salt to the earth. He just wanted cool it.
One of the guys in the band.

Yeah and it made it wonderful for us because I‟m here and he is over there and Katherine has got this big Olympic swimming pool and a cabana and all that and she would invite all these big clubs and National Conference of Christians and Jews and she had [unintelligible] donors of Africa to have their fashion shows over there. Basie, if he is home, he don‟t want to be bothered with that. So Mona is over there helping Katherine and Basie would come over here and he and I would sit down in the basement and we would have a little taste. He loved Charlie Chaplain movies and I had some of the Charlie Chaplain silent movies so I would put them on. I had an upright piano that Teddy Wilson had gotten for me and it was down in the basement. Basie would sit there and look at those films for a little while and pretty soon he would sit down at the piano, da, da, da. He would play it a little faster to go with the movie. And we would sit there and have a great time like that. Our relationship was warm and so when he asked me to come and work with him, I said, “Well look I just come off the road and I don‟t want to go on the road. I am trying to get me some gigs in town.” He said, “I think I am going to be in town, why don‟t you come and play with me while I‟m around town. I said, “Well I will do that as long as you pick me up since you are right here and take me to work with you and when we get through, you bring home. And if you get a chick, you better get through because if I go home without you we are both in trouble.” So it was a really wonderful relationship. We would get through at night and he would drive us home. We would stop on Queen‟s Boulevard and he would say, “Let‟ stop at the Steak House.” It was in White Tower.
